```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", echo = FALSE)
sim <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "simulation.rds", package = "flexsae"))
fmt <- function(x, d = 3) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d)
pt <- sim$point[sim$point$areas == "sampled", ]
rt <- function(sc, m) fmt(pt$ratio_fh[pt$scenario == sc & pt$method == m])
rng <- function(scs, m) {
  x <- pt$ratio_fh[pt$scenario %in% scs & pt$method == m]
  paste(fmt(min(x)), "to", fmt(max(x)))
}
ms <- function(m, col, d = 3) {
  x <- sim$mse[sim$mse$method == m, col]
  paste(fmt(min(x), d), "to", fmt(max(x), d))
}
b_scs <- grep("^B", sim$scenarios$scenario, value = TRUE)
```

This article reports a simulation study of the models of flexsae against the
linear Fay-Herriot model, following the ADEMP structure (aims, data-generating
mechanisms, estimands, methods, performance measures). The results are
precomputed by `benchmarks/simulation/run.R` (flexsae `r sim$settings$flexsae`,
`r sim$settings$R_version`) and summarised by
`benchmarks/update_benchmark_docs.R`; every number has its Monte Carlo
standard error (MCSE).

## Design

**Aims.** Accuracy of the area estimates against the linear Fay-Herriot model
when the covariate effects are linear or not; quality of the bootstrap MSE and
of the intervals; computing time.

**Data-generating mechanisms.** Area-level model
\(\theta_d = f(x_d) + v_d\), \(y_d = \theta_d + e_d\), \(e_d \sim N(0, \psi_d)\),
with \(\sigma^2_v = 1\) and \(\psi_d = \bar\psi\,U(0.5, 1.5)\),
\(\bar\psi = \sigma^2_v/\text{ratio}\). The covariates are drawn once per
scenario (fixed design); \(v_d\) and \(e_d\) are redrawn in every replicate.

| Shape | \(f(x)\) | Covariates in the models |
|---|---|---|
| B (linear) | \(1 + x_1 + 0.5x_2\) | \(x_1, x_2\) |
| A1 (quadratic) | \(1 + 0.8x_1^2 + 0.5x_2\) | \(x_1, x_2\) |
| A2 (sine) | \(1 + 1.5\sin(1.5x_1) + 0.5x_2\) | \(x_1, x_2\) |
| A3 (threshold) | \(1 + 1.5\,\mathbb{1}(x_1 > 0) + 0.5x_2\) | \(x_1, x_2\) |
| A4 (interaction) | \(1 + 0.8x_1x_2 + 0.5x_2\) | \(x_1, x_2\) |
| A5 (Bukhari et al., 2026, eq. 20) | \(x_1^2 + 2x_2^3 + 3\log(\lvert x_3\rvert + 1) + 4\log\lvert x_4\rvert\) | \(x_1, \dots, x_4\) |
| C (mixed) | \(1 + 1.5\sin(1.5x_1) + 0.8x_2^2 + 0.5x_3\) | \(x_1, \dots, x_8\): five noise covariates, two correlated with \(x_1\) and \(x_3\) |

\(x \sim U(-2, 2)\), except A5 (\(U(0.5, 2)\), our choice: the paper's text does
not give the covariate distribution). The base setting has \(D = 100\) areas
and ratio 1. For B and A2 one factor at a time is varied: \(D \in \{30, 50,
300\}\), ratio \(\in \{0.25, 4\}\), \(\psi_d\) in five groups
(\(\bar\psi \times \{0.1, 0.3, 0.8, 1.3, 2.5\}\)), \(v_d\) from a scaled \(t_3\),
and 10% unsampled areas; A2 also with half the non-linearity
(\(\lambda = 0.5\)). All shapes except A5 are our own designs.

**Estimand.** \(\theta_d\) for every area.

**Methods.** Direct estimator; linear Fay-Herriot model, REML, from
`sae::eblupFH()` (with \(x^\prime\hat\beta\) for unsampled areas);
`pspline_sae()` with `s(x, k = 8)` for every covariate (`k = 5` for
\(D \le 50\)); `merf_sae()` with `variant = "replace"` and `"correct"`
(algorithm `"fhrf"`, 500 trees) and the experimental `algorithm = "merf"`;
BART-FH from `nlfh::fit_fh_bart()` with its defaults (sampled areas only).

**Performance.** For each replicate, the mean over the areas of the squared
error; its mean over the replicates, and the ratio to the linear Fay-Herriot
model (paired replicates, delta-method MCSE). MSE study (five scenarios): the
relative bias of the MSE estimator per area, coverage and width of the 95%
intervals. Bootstrap with \(B = `r sim$settings$B`\).

**Replicates.** `r sim$settings$R_point` per scenario for the point
estimates and `r sim$settings$R_mse` for the MSE study; one L'Ecuyer-CMRG
stream per replicate.

## Summary

- **Linear truth (scenarios B).** `pspline_sae()` is close to the linear
  Fay-Herriot model (ratio `r rng(b_scs, "pspline")`), because the smooths
  shrink to straight lines. The random forest of `merf_sae()` costs accuracy
  when the truth is linear (`"correct"`: `r rng(b_scs, "merf_correct")`;
  `"replace"`: `r rng(b_scs, "merf_replace")`), most with large sampling
  variances (ratio 0.25) and few areas. Prefer the linear model or
  `pspline_sae()` when there is no sign of non-linearity.
- **Non-linear truth.** `pspline_sae()` gains most for smooth additive
  effects (quadratic `r rt("A1", "pspline")`, sine `r rt("A2", "pspline")`,
  mixed `r rt("C", "pspline")`, Bukhari et al.'s function
  `r rt("A5", "pspline")`). `merf_sae()` gains less (sine
  `r rt("A2", "merf_replace")`) but more for the interaction A4, which an
  additive spline model cannot represent (`r rt("A4", "merf_replace")` against
  `r rt("A4", "pspline")`). Gains are below 1% for the step function A3
  (`r rt("A3", "pspline")` and `r rt("A3", "merf_replace")`) and absent with
  \(D = 30\).
- **`variant = "replace"` against `"correct"`.** On the function of Bukhari
  et al. (A5) `"replace"` is worse than the linear model
  (`r rt("A5", "merf_replace")`) and `"correct"` better
  (`r rt("A5", "merf_correct")`). A likely reason, not checked: with our
  covariate design (the paper does not give its own) the terms are close to
  linear, which the linear part of `"correct"` captures and a forest
  approximates with steps.
- **Experimental `algorithm = "merf"`.** Better than `"fhrf"` for A1 and A4,
  worse in most other scenarios; it stays experimental.
- **MSE.** The bootstrap MSE of `pspline_sae()` is slightly too small (median
  relative bias `r ms("pspline", "rb_median")`) with coverage slightly below
  95% (`r ms("pspline", "coverage")`); that of `merf_sae()` is conservative
  when the truth is non-linear (median relative bias up to
  `r fmt(max(sim$mse$rb_median[sim$mse$method == "merf_replace"]))`, coverage
  `r ms("merf_replace", "coverage")`).
- **Cost.** With the bootstrap, `pspline_sae()` is much slower than
  `merf_sae()` (last table), because every replicate refits the mixed
  model with mgcv.

## Accuracy

Ratio of the mean squared error to the linear Fay-Herriot model (below 1:
more accurate), sampled areas, with MCSE in parentheses.

```{r ratio-table}
p <- sim$point[sim$point$areas == "sampled", ]
methods <- c("pspline", "merf_replace", "merf_correct", "merf_iterative", "bart_fh", "direct")
labels <- c("pspline", "merf replace", "merf correct", "merf iterative", "BART-FH", "direct")
tab <- data.frame(scenario = unique(p$scenario))
for (i in seq_along(methods)) {
  m <- p[p$method == methods[i], ]
  tab[[labels[i]]] <- ifelse(is.na(match(tab$scenario, m$scenario)), "",
    paste0(fmt(m$ratio_fh[match(tab$scenario, m$scenario)]), " (",
           fmt(m$ratio_mcse[match(tab$scenario, m$scenario)]), ")"))
}
ord <- match(sim$scenarios$scenario, tab$scenario)
tab <- tab[ord[!is.na(ord)], ]
knitr::kable(tab, row.names = FALSE)
```

### Where flexsae is not better

Scenarios in which a flexsae model has a mean squared error above the linear
Fay-Herriot model by more than two MCSE:

```{r losses}
fl <- p[p$method %in% c("pspline", "merf_replace", "merf_correct", "merf_iterative"), ]
loss <- fl[fl$ratio_fh - 2 * fl$ratio_mcse > 1, c("scenario", "method", "ratio_fh", "ratio_mcse")]
loss$ratio_fh <- fmt(loss$ratio_fh)
loss$ratio_mcse <- fmt(loss$ratio_mcse)
if (nrow(loss) == 0) cat("None.\n") else knitr::kable(loss, row.names = FALSE)
```

### Unsampled areas

```{r unsampled}
u <- sim$point[sim$point$areas == "unsampled", c("scenario", "method", "ratio_fh", "ratio_mcse")]
u$ratio_fh <- fmt(u$ratio_fh)
u$ratio_mcse <- fmt(u$ratio_mcse)
knitr::kable(u, row.names = FALSE)
```

## MSE estimation and intervals

```{r mse-table}
m <- sim$mse
out <- data.frame(
  scenario = m$scenario, method = m$method,
  `RB median` = fmt(m$rb_median), `RB P10-P90` = paste0(fmt(m$rb_p10, 2), " to ", fmt(m$rb_p90, 2)),
  coverage = paste0(fmt(m$coverage), " (", fmt(m$coverage_mcse), ")"),
  width = fmt(m$width), check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(out, row.names = FALSE)
```

RB is the relative bias of the MSE estimator of an area,
\((\overline{\widehat{\mathrm{mse}}}_d - \mathrm{MSE}_d)/\mathrm{MSE}_d\), with
\(\mathrm{MSE}_d\) the Monte Carlo MSE. The linear Fay-Herriot MSE is the
Prasad-Rao estimator (`sae::mseFH()`); BART-FH intervals are posterior
quantiles.

## Computing time

Mean seconds per fit for scenario B: point estimates with \(D = 100\) and
\(D = 300\), and with the bootstrap MSE (\(B = `r sim$settings$B`\); Prasad-Rao for
the linear model, posterior sampling for BART-FH). Ten fits ran in parallel,
so single fits are faster. In this run the times of the linear model and of
BART-FH include loading the packages sae and nlfh in every replicate (each
replicate ran in a fresh process); a single `sae::eblupFH()` fit with
\(D = 100\) takes milliseconds.

```{r time}
tt <- data.frame(method = unique(p$method[p$scenario == "B"]))
pick <- function(d, sc) {
  x <- d$time[match(paste(sc, tt$method), paste(d$scenario, d$method))]
  ifelse(is.na(x), "", fmt(x, 2))
}
tt$`D = 100` <- pick(p, "B")
tt$`D = 300` <- pick(p, "B_D300")
tt$`D = 100, with MSE` <- pick(sim$mse, "B")
knitr::kable(tt, row.names = FALSE)
```

estimation. *Ingénierie des Systèmes d'Information*, 31(6), 1811-1823.
https://doi.org/10.18280/isi.310604

Morris, T. P., White, I. R. and Crowther, M. J. (2019). Using simulation
